cls_provenance.why_reversed: The controls taken (home 0.2412, search 0.4616) are DIFFERENT ROUTES, not the same route on the pre-PR theme — and this PR is a full rewrite of /compare, so a high CLS elsewhere is no evidence that this page's 0.12 predates it. The instrument is wrong too: this run itself established that CLS CANNOT see the 144px morph shift because hadRecentInput excludes it, so CLS cannot then be used to dismiss a finding on the same surface. The numbers appeared in no artifact. The control that settles it is /compare on the base theme, and it was not taken.

severity_regrade.why: CMP-003 carries Priority=Critical in the CSV and the model rates scenario 3 Critical (functional loss, not styling). Grading the finding Medium contradicted both and left every in-scope finding at P2 — under which the framework verdict would have been PASS WITH NOTES. The verdict no longer depends on this (five unbuilt promises settle it on volume), but the grade was wrong on its own terms.

verdict_framing.but_communicate_as: incomplete delivery against the description, NOT defective implementation
verdict_framing.why: Six of ten description bullets are wholly or partly unimplemented. 'Defective' routes to a bug-fix cycle (reproduce, fix, re-verify); 'incomplete' routes back to the story's own scope — to the PM and designer, and to whether this story was finishable as written. A bug-shaped comment sends a scope conversation to the wrong people. The token stays FAIL because nothing downstream recognises a new one, and inventing one breaks the gate math and the release-note refusal logic.
verdict_framing.root_cause: The Story reached READY FOR TEST with its acceptance-criteria field reading '1. No requirements.' That is the mechanism that let six of ten described behaviours go unbuilt with nobody noticing — there was no artifact anyone could check done against. Everything downstream inherited it: 1d had to derive 74 conditions from prose, the verdict is scoped to a spec the ticket does not contain, and the checklist carries a disclaimer saying so. No amount of testing downstream fixes that.

hypotheses_grounded.claim: at 375px both Clear all and Clear category are PRESENT in the DOM but computed display:none (the wrapper for Clear all, the button itself for Clear category); no overflow menu exists anywhere; per-product removal survives and Restore is desktop-gated because it lives only in the empty state. This is a responsive-visibility stylesheet defect, NOT an unimplemented feature — corrected at the Step-3 gate by a computed-style check on a second browser lane after an earlier reading said absent-from-DOM.

3 plain products with divergent min/max/available painted fully and stayed interactive with zero Vue warnings. CAVEAT: production build, where the recursive-update warning is dev-only, so the warning could not appear either way. The write-during-render pattern is NOT settled and needs a unit test.

the clamp is enforced at ADD time — the 6th add is refused with a toast 'Only 5 products from the same category can be compared'; the ghost state is unreachable via the UI. A pre-existing over-limit payload was NOT probed.
Restore exists only in the empty state and any add removes it, so Restore and a non-empty list cannot coexist. Clear all is additionally confirmation-gated.

OBSERVED live: under Differences the Availability row is displayed with two cells both reading 9999+. MECHANISM: authoring re-read PR-head source and found price and availability are PERMANENT_ROW_KEYS, shown under Differences by design — which already explains the observation. getAvailabilitySignature also caps at the same threshold the cell renders, so those two stocks yield an IDENTICAL signature. So neither 1c raw-vs-formatted reading nor the 3x inference is established; the customer-visible complaint is real, the mechanism is the permanent-row rule, and raw-vs-capped is UNSETTLED. CMP-010 asserts only the invariant that can bite: no NON-permanent surviving row may render two indistinguishable cells.

sources: 4 .vue files in the diff including a new 689-line compare-table.vue
the ticket is a design redesign with a Figma link and a Claude Design prototype

invariant_failures.summary: the sticky full-to-compact morph shifts the table body 144px in one frame at desktop (header 251->107, first row top 419->235 where scroll accounts for only 40, document height -144)
invariant_failures.note: CLS CANNOT see it — the shift falls within 500ms of a keypress so hadRecentInput excludes it. The 0.051 CLS pass must not be read as shift-free.

invariant_failures.summary: the compact morph never fires below md (767px stuck=false h=211.8 vs 768px stuck=true h=107), so at 375px the pinned header holds 211.8px — ~35% of a 600px viewport — with data rows rendering underneath it

At 375px Pin, Clear all AND Clear category all vanish together — ONE hidden-below-md rule dropping the entire secondary-action set, reached identically by viewport (CMP-003) and by browser zoom (CMP-031). The single folded report must be written as the whole secondary-action set, not as two clear controls.

advisory.note: the prototype derives categories from a hardcoded title/vendor regex while the implementation uses breadcrumbs at depth 2, so tab labels will not match the prototype — expected, never a failure
the prototype renders a Share button beside Clear all; the implementation omits it. The ticket never asked for Share, so its absence is correct w.r.t. the ticket and a divergence w.r.t. the spec

the root 'Compare v2 - standalone.html' is a bundled prototype whose declared values are not statically extractable; recorded unresolved rather than guessed. ui_kits/storefront/CompareScreenV2.jsx was used as the spec source instead.

The diff-marking finding was previously recorded here as UNSPEC on the grounds that the PROTOTYPE renders no dot/amber row. That was wrong and it laundered an in-scope defect into a bucket that can never fail 5c: the TICKET is the oracle, and bullet 3 promises the marking in the ticket own words. Moved to unbuilt_promises below as an IN-SCOPE finding.

unverified.condition: V3 (BL-UI-005) column alignment between the header and body tables
unverified.reason: The PASS was measured at desktop with both scrollers at zero. The two tables are INDEPENDENT scrollers with different geometry (header client 234 / scroll 448 vs body client 346 / scroll 560), which is the precondition for the sticky header drifting out of column alignment on mobile. Re-verify at 375px with the body scrolled, or leave it unverified — do not carry a BL-UI-005 PASS resting on a desktop-only measurement.

a11y_findings.summary: the table body cannot be scrolled by keyboard at <=767px — scrollWidth 560 > clientWidth 361, 0 focusable descendants, no tabindex, no role, no accessible name
inactive All/Differences segment measures 4.34:1 (needs 4.5) at 14px bold — light mode only, dark passes
All/Differences exposes no selected state (role, aria-pressed, aria-checked all null); the category tabs DO carry aria-pressed, which is the tell
focus indicators at 1.47:1 (pin) and about 1.9:1 (breadcrumb, Clear category) — shared vc-button ring, cross-cutting on the UI kit

header and body are two separate table elements so scope=col cannot associate across them, and every table element is overridden to block/flex. ECL-15.1 notes this violates no BL-A11Y rule as written — PROPOSED-BL candidate
info tooltip is not keyboard-operable; the tip text still reaches AT via the inner span aria-label, so no information is lost
a11y_findings.subsumed_by: the bullet-7 functional finding — the SAME DOM fact (the trigger is absent below md). File the functional one, cross-link this, do not file both.

a11y_findings.summary: two category tabs share an identical accessible name, ambiguous to sighted and AT users alike
pin and info are hidden below md and browser zoom crosses md, so at 400% a desktop user loses pinning and tooltips
a11y_findings.note: THIS ONE BLOCKS and is deliberately NOT filed as a separate a11y ticket: it is the same stylesheet rule as CMP-003/CMP-031 and folds into that in-scope report. Recorded here so the fold is auditable rather than looking like a dropped a11y finding.

status_transitions.why_late: The opening-hop rule (knowledge/execution/ticket-status-transitions.md, and the 1a instruction in commands/qa-test.md) landed MID-RUN — both files were written at 17:28, hours after this run read qa-test.md at 1a. So the run was compliant with the command as it stood when it routed, and non-compliant with the command as it stands now. Recovered under §7, which requires a run that skipped the opening hop to make it at 5f before closing: on Jira neither REOPEN nor TESTED is reachable from Ready for test — the live transition list from that status offered only On QA, go to inprogress, Cancelled and On hold.
status_transitions.cost: The ticket read as unclaimed on the board for the whole run — roughly 10 agent dispatches, 35 authored cases, a seeded fixture set and two verifier gates — which is the precise failure the rule was written against. 1b's duplicate check guards only against THIS pipeline re-testing the ticket inside 2h; it does not stop a human picking it up.
